name: Atomic Wallet
rootCause: Atomic Wallet blew up earlier this month. Even after two weeks, no official root cause has been announced, and the team's past attitude to security raises concerns. Will they ever admit what went wrong? Do they even know?

descriptions.text: Atomic Wallet blew up earlier this month. Even after two weeks, no official root cause has been announced, and the team's past attitude to security raises concerns. Will they ever admit what went wrong? Do they even know?

On June 3, multiple Atomic Wallet users posted on social media that their wallet assets had been stolen. Atomic says less than 1% of monthly active users are currently affected/reported. According to SlowMist, Atomic Wallet officially offlined cloudflare’s download site and sha256sum verification site in an emergency. From this, it is speculated that there may be a security problem in the link of downloading the historical version. It is reported that this incident is suspected to be related to the North Korean hacker group Lazarus Group.

Atomic Wallet suffered a massive breach in June 2023, with attackers acquiring user private keys and draining ~$100M across eight blockchains. The exact vulnerability,possibly supply-chain compromise, weak key generation, or server exposure,was never confirmed. Thousands of wallets were drained simultaneously; most assets remain unrecovered. Attackers gained access to users' private keys or seed phrases by compromising Atomic Wallet's application-level security. Proposed causes include supply-chain attack with malicious updates, weak random number generation enabling brute-force of key material, or server-side exposure of keys. The precise entry point was never published by Atomic Wallet.

In June 2023, Atomic Wallet experienced a mass compromise affecting thousands of users across multiple blockchains, resulting in estimated losses between $35 million and $100 million. The attack was likely due to a supply chain compromise or critical vulnerability in client-side key handling, enabling extraction of private keys and synchronized fund drains. In June 2023, Atomic Wallet suffered a large-scale security breach, with at least $35 million stolen from thousands of users across several blockchains. The precise technical cause remains undisclosed, but attribution to North Korea’s Lazarus Group is strongly supported by blockchain tracing. Theories include supply chain compromise and key extraction vulnerabilities, but no confirmed exploit path is publicly available. The technical root cause of the Atomic Wallet incident has not been publicly determined. External analysis suggests possible causes such as supply chain attack or flaws in local key management, but no single exploit mechanism has been established.

Multiple users of the Atomic Wallet software suffered wallet compromises totaling more than $100 million in a spate of hacks suggesting an issue with the wallet itself. Atomic Wallet is a self-custody wallet, a suggested safer alternative than storing crypto assets in accounts controlled by third party companies. In February 2022, a security firm was forced to publicly disclose issues with the Atomic Wallet software after attempting to address them with the company via traditional routes, but went ignored.
